candidates.api_shape: toggle_joint(bar_a, bar_b, stroke, knee_deg) -> {bar_a, bar_b, ram} plus MA=1/tan(theta)
candidates.fdm: Two bars, three pins, a sliding ram. Prints flat. 507 #140 without the punching frame. Pose is knee angle; lock past 0.
candidates.name: toggle_joint
candidates.why: The generic over-center cell. toggle_clamp is a hold-down with a handle and a toe. This is the force-amplifier agents reinvent for presses, locks, and folding legs.

candidates.api_shape: knuckle_press(crank_r, rod, rocker, push, phase_deg) -> {crank, rod, rockers, push_rods, ram} plus ram_z(theta)
candidates.fdm: Crank + conrod + two rockers + two push rods + ram. Prints as bars. Long dwell near BDC. Schuler class.
candidates.name: knuckle_press
candidates.why: The named press drive. slider_crank is a punch without the force spike. toggle_joint is the last two bars. This is the whole 1-DoF cell, not a C-frame machine.

candidates.api_shape: knee_lever(bar_a, bar_b, lever_len, lever_deg) -> {bars, lever, ram} 507 #164
candidates.fdm: A toggle whose knee is lifted by a horizontal lever. Prints. One-shot stamp / press.
candidates.name: knee_lever
candidates.why: 507's other named toggle. Hand-driven, not crank-driven. Distinct from knuckle_press (continuous rotation) and from toggle_clamp (clamps, does not stamp).

candidates.api_shape: disk_bar_press(disk_d, bar_len, n_bars=2, rot_deg) -> {top_disk, bars, platen}
candidates.fdm: Two disks, two (or more) bars in holes. Top disk turns, bars go upright, platen drops. 507 #132. Prints.
candidates.name: disk_bar_press
candidates.why: Oblique bars between disks. Not a planar toggle and not a screw. Named 507 press, unused elsewhere in the survey.

candidates.api_shape: two toggles in series or mirrored, one ram
candidates.fdm: Four bars, one ram. Prints. Coining / sizing presses. After toggle_joint this is a thin composition.
candidates.name: double_toggle
candidates.why: Two knees, more MA, more dwell. Useful as a named kit once toggle_joint exists; do not ship it first.

candidates.api_shape: pinion + toothed sector + rod to a platen, 507 #133
candidates.fdm: Already compose from spur_gear_sector + a rod.
candidates.name: sector_press
candidates.why: A sector and a connecting rod. No new pair. Skip unless someone wants the named 507 demo.

candidates.api_shape: a flywheel on a vertical screw, 507 #105
candidates.fdm: lead_screw + flywheel. The ball handles are product trim.
candidates.name: screw_stamp
candidates.why: Flying / screw stamp. The primitives exist. A named kit is optional teaching only.

candidates.name: toggle_clamp_again
candidates.why: Already the over-center workholding knee. Do not claim it twice.

candidates.name: scissor_jack_again
candidates.why: A screw shortens an X. Different law from a toggle (no over-center lock). Ship it under linear.

candidates.name: draw_hood_latch_again
candidates.why: Panel locks on the toggle law. Other slice owns them.

candidates.fdm: C-frame, bolster, clutch, brake, die set.
candidates.name: punch_press_product
candidates.why: A finished machine. The cell is knuckle_press or slider_crank.

rejected.name: vise_grip
rejected.why: Locking pliers are a product around toggle_joint. The cell is enough.

rejected.name: bistable_as_toggle
rejected.why: bistable_beam is a compliant snap-through. Different physics, already in-tree.

sources: mechlib/linkages.py toggle_clamp lazy_tongs slider_crank, mechlib/linear.py screw_jack lead_screw, mechlib/flexures.py bistable_beam, .claude/overnight/gaps/grippers-chucks-workholding.json draw_latch hood_latch, .claude/overnight/gaps/screws-linear-actuators.json scissor_jack
summary:
A toggle is two bars sharing a knee that is driven toward colinearity. Mechanical advantage goes to infinity as the knee straightens; past dead centre the cell locks (over-center). 507 names the toggle-joint as a punching machine (140) and a knee-lever press (164). Norton and every press-builder split mechanical presses by the last joint: crank/slider (slider_crank already), knuckle/toggle (missing), screw (lead_screw / screw_jack), and hydraulic (product). Schuler's knuckle-joint press is a crank that drives a two-bar toggle into the ram, giving a long dwell and a huge force near BDC. 507 #132 is a different cell: two oblique bars between disks that go upright when the top disk turns. #105 is a screw stamp. #133 is a pinion-and-sector platen.

Catalog already has one over-center product-shaped kit: toggle_clamp (welding hold-down, posed). grippers already proposed draw_latch and hood_latch (panel locks on the same law). screws-linear already proposed scissor_jack (screw shortens an X). bistable_beam is a compliant snap-through, not a bar toggle. lazy_tongs is a rhomb chain that extends, not a force amplifier. Grep of mechlib/ finds no toggle_joint, knuckle_press, or knee_lever. A punch-press frame, a fly press with a ball, or a vise-grip plier is a product.

FDM reality. toggle_joint is two bars and a driven knee, ram on the far pin; pose is knee angle, MA = 1/tan(theta). Prints flat. This is the missing primitive under toggle_clamp. knuckle_press is a crank + connecting rod + two rockers + two push rods + ram (the usual Schuler inversion); pose is crank angle, ram z and a dwell near BDC. knee_lever is 507 #164, a horizontal lever that lifts the knee, a one-shot stamp. disk_bar_press is 507 #132, two (or more) bars between a grounded disk and a turning disk; unique, not a four_bar. double_toggle is two toggles in series or in parallel, the coining-press default. Do not re-rank toggle_clamp, scissor_jack, or the latches. Do not emit a C-frame press.
title: Toggle joints, over-center, and press cells
